decision.title: Q4 routing decision
decision.author: human
decision.body:
## Situation

Night transit restrictions are announced from 1 October; Q4 cargoes are booked.

## Trigger

The wire report of 14 September.

## Conditions

Restrictions are evidenced by one origin only; nothing on the board refutes them.

## Facts

One evidenced report, repeated by two media (one origin). Insurance quotes rose
fast last time.

## Priorities

Delivery reliability before freight cost.

## Action

Reroute the next three laden tankers via the Cape of Good Hope.

## Alternatives

Hold course with war-risk cover; delay sailings by two weeks.

## Exclusions

No night transits while restrictions apply.

## Rationale

My reroute rule fires; the cost of delay outweighs the extra distance.

## Cards used

- 01M1E34QM03WVTE8T1RYS3AM18
- 01M1EDEAG082WZ7T7D204BHZDC
- 01M1EMA1R0AH9ZTK3YJK33TNER

## Outcome

open

usedCards.title: Wire report announces transit restrictions in the strait
usedCards.author: human
usedCards.body:
A (fictional) wire agency reports that the coastal state will restrict night
transits of laden tankers through the strait from 1 October.

This card is the origin of the provenance chain in this example: the two
media cards below only repeat it.

usedCards.title: Last time, war-risk quotes jumped within a day
usedCards.author: human
usedCards.body:
Own (invented) experience: during an earlier tension phase, war-risk
insurance quotes for the strait rose sharply within one day of the first
announcement.
